svg.text: Crow's-foot notation. Foreign keys are ObjectId references checked in application code; MongoDB does not enforce them.
collection (one model for all three roles)
foreign key: ObjectId reference to another collection
MongoDB stores documents in collections, not rows in tables.
Only these constraints exist in the database:
unique index users.email, unique index jobs.slug,
Every foreign key above is a Mongoose reference that the
code resolves with populate(); deleting a user, company or
job removes related documents in code, not by cascade rules.
applications.company duplicates jobs.company so a company
statusHistory[] is embedded in each application document;
it is not a separate collection.
users holds all roles; the role field and the applicant /
company / admin columns decide which fields are used.
